fields.description: ERPNext Upload = the bytes are in the private File below, under this app's permission model. Drive Link = a Google Drive file the picker returned; the bytes stay in Drive under Drive's own ACL and Triton reads them with the user's OWN Google credential. Copying Drive bytes into ERPNext would re-home somebody else's sharing decision inside ours and there is no way to un-make that later.
fields.label: Source

fields.description: The original filename as the user saw it, never a path.
fields.label: File Name

fields.description: Guessed from the stored filename SERVER-SIDE. A client-declared content type is not evidence, so it is never stored.
fields.label: Content Type

fields.description: Size in bytes, read off the File row rather than off the request. File.file_size is set from a client-supplied form field on upload, so this is a record, not an enforcement point -- the ceiling is enforced against the bytes on disk in register_upload().
fields.label: File Size

fields.description: The private File row holding the bytes. This row is its attached_to_name, which is what makes the file readable at all: an ORPHAN private File is readable only through File.has_permission's `doc.owner == user` shortcut, which is a per-uploader accident rather than a policy, and nothing in core ever garbage-collects one. Attached here, it inherits this row's has_permission hook and is deleted with it by delete_doc's remove_all(). Empty for a Drive Link.
fields.label: File

fields.description: The Drive file id the browser picker returned. ERPNext never fetches it: the app's only Drive client is a SERVICE ACCOUNT with no domain-wide delegation, which 404s on a file nobody explicitly shared with it -- i.e. on exactly the personal document this feature exists to serve. Triton reads it with the picking user's own stored OAuth credential (gws_get_file_content).
fields.label: Drive File ID

fields.description: The picker's webViewLink. Validated on write to be https on a Google host -- it is rendered as an href in the widget's chip.
fields.label: Drive URL

fields.description: Triton's own chat session id -- an integer in Triton's database, not a Frappe Link, because the conversation does not exist in ERPNext at all. Blank until the turn carrying this attachment is actually sent.
fields.label: Triton Session

fields.description: When this attachment was first handed to the model. Blank means it is still a pending chip in somebody's composer, and the daily sweep deletes those after 24 hours -- a chip attached and never sent is abandoned, not archived.
fields.label: Used At

fields.description: Retention cut-off, stamped at creation. Time-based expiry is not laziness: Triton owns the conversation, so ERPNext can never observe a chat being deleted and has no other GC signal.
fields.label: Expires On
